## Introduction

`selectFiberseqLociWorkflow` is a native R package for analyzing processed
Fiber-seq tracks at selected loci. Analysis runs directly in R. Regions use
`GRanges`; each locus is a `RangedSummarizedExperiment` with genomic positions
in rows and individual reads in columns. This vignette uses the same ALAS1
region and two tutorial LCL samples for both clustering choices.

The bundled data contain up to 100 full-span reads per sample per region,
with complete matching m6A, nucleosome, TF-footprint and FIRE records. The
small subset has 18 full-span reads at ALAS1 and 16 at PRDX1. It demonstrates
usage and numerical consistency; it is not a biological replicate study.
The data provenance and reproducible subset-generation script accompany the
package. No allele-specific inputs or topic modelling are used.

## Load the package and writable example

```{r libraries}
library(selectFiberseqLociWorkflow)
library(SummarizedExperiment)
library(GenomicRanges)
```

```{r input}
example <- example_data()
example$samples[, c("sample_name", "sample_label", "m6a_format", "tf_format")]
alas1 <- example$regions["ALAS1"]
alas1
validate_inputs(example$samples, alas1)
```

The input region covers chr3:52197160-52199159, with a TSS at 52198160
(one-based inclusive). File formats are explicit. The package does not infer
whether tracks came from fibertools or FiberHMM.

## Analyze without clustering

Choose `clustering` explicitly. Reads are retained only if their longest
alignment spans the whole selected window, including reads with no m6A calls.
The assay is sparse and binary: zero means no observed m6A call at that base,
not a direct measurement that every base is an unmethylated adenine.

```{r unclustered}
unclustered <- analyze_loci(example$samples, alas1, clustering = FALSE)[[1]]
unclustered
colData(unclustered)[, c("sample_name", "original_RID", "start", "end")]
```

### Interoperability and coordinate consistency

All in-memory coordinates are one-based inclusive. BED starts are converted
once at import. `rowRanges` identifies each assay row; `colData` identifies
its corresponding read column. Read alignments are `GRanges`, and footprints
are grouped by read in a `GRangesList` column of `colData`.

```{r containers}
rowRanges(unclustered)[1:3]
colData(unclustered)$read_range[1:3]
colData(unclustered)$footprints[1]
small <- unclustered[1:20, c(3, 1)]
stopifnot(identical(colnames(small), rownames(colData(small))),
    identical(colnames(small), colData(small)$RID),
    identical(names(rowRanges(small)), rownames(small)))
small
```

Subsetting keeps read metadata, alignment ranges and footprints aligned with
assay columns. Footprints describe the retained read within the original
locus; row subsetting does not clip these stored intervals. Original QC,
parameters and the cluster graph remain in `metadata` as run provenance.
`locus_profile()` recalculates fractions for the current columns.

### Unclustered views

Rows in the heatmap follow sample-sheet order, alignment start and read ID.
The heatmap displays reads vertically and positions horizontally even though
the underlying experiment uses the standard features-by-observations layout.

```{r unclustered-heatmap, fig.height=6}
ComplexHeatmap::draw(plot_locus(unclustered, "heatmap"))
```

The pooled fraction divides by all full-span reads, including zero-call reads.
Grey shows observed-position fractions; the colored curve uses the tutorial
10-bp sliding-window mean. The dashed line marks the supplied TSS.

```{r unclustered-profile}
plot_locus(unclustered, "profile")
head(locus_profile(unclustered))
```

Optional tracks use nucleosomes of 130-160 bp and TF footprints in [10,30),
[40,60), or [60,80) bp. FiberHMM TF blocks require a score of at least 50.
A supplied footprint track with no retained calls raises the warning
`no footprints called in the selected region`; the analysis still completes.

```{r unclustered-footprints, fig.height=8}
plot_locus(unclustered, "footprints")
```

## Analyze the same locus with clustering

Clustering uses observed m6A positions, Manhattan distances, a nearest-neighbor
graph and Leiden communities. It does not change the input read set, sparse
assay, pooled denominators or unclustered plots. The seed and all parameters
are saved with the experiment. Exact pairwise distances require memory
quadratic in the number of reads, so select suitably sized loci and datasets.

```{r clustered}
clustered <- analyze_loci(example$samples, alas1, clustering = TRUE,
    k_neighbors = 10, resolution = 1, seed = 1)[[1]]
stopifnot(identical(assay(unclustered), assay(clustered)),
    identical(colnames(unclustered), colnames(clustered)),
    identical(locus_profile(unclustered), locus_profile(clustered)))
table(colData(clustered)$sample_label, colData(clustered)$cluster)
metadata(clustered)$clustering_status
```

```{r clustered-heatmap, fig.height=6}
ComplexHeatmap::draw(plot_locus(clustered, "heatmap", clustered = TRUE))
```

```{r clustered-profile}
plot_locus(clustered, "profile", clustered = TRUE)
```

```{r clustered-footprints, fig.height=8}
plot_locus(clustered, "footprints", clustered = TRUE)
```

Cluster plots only reorder reads or split profile denominators by existing
cluster assignments. If a locus has fewer than three reads or two occupied
features, clustering is skipped with a reason in `metadata`.

## Export and reload

One call writes both views for this clustered result, alongside the complete
Bioconductor object. The `unclustered` directory remains independent of
clustering parameters. RDS files preserve the explicit clustering choice for
later plotting; re-analysis requires a new explicit choice.

```{r export}
output <- tempfile("alas1-output-")
write_locus_results(clustered, output)
list.files(output, recursive = TRUE)
restored <- readRDS(file.path(output, "ALAS1", "locus.rds"))
stopifnot(identical(assay(restored), assay(clustered)))
```

## User data and plant annotations

Create a sample sheet with `make_sample_sheet(data.frame(...))`. Required
columns are `sample_name`, `m6a` and `m6a_format`; optional tracks have their own
explicit format columns. Paths can use `{sample_name}` and `{chr}` templates.
Use bgzip-compressed tracks with adjacent tabix indexes and exact matching
contig names from the same genome assembly. The package expects processed
tracks; it does not call fibertools or FiberHMM itself.

`prepare_regions()` accepts `GRanges`, BED files, one-based inclusive coordinate
strings, coordinate tables with declared conventions, or GTF/GFF3 transcript
annotations. Ordinary annotation extraction retains distinct TSSs and does
not require canonical transcripts. Promoter flanks default to 1,000 bp.

```{r plant-annotations}
annotation <- system.file("extdata", "plant", "annotation.gff3",
    package = "selectFiberseqLociWorkflow")
plant_regions <- prepare_regions(annotation = annotation)
plant_regions
prepare_regions("scaffold_42:4001-6000")
extract_canonical_tss(annotation, genes = "AT5G00010",
    attribute = "canonical", value = "true")
```

The synthetic fixture includes `Chr5`, `scaffold_42`, both strands, shared and
distinct transcript TSSs, and genes without canonical tags. It verifies format
and coordinate compatibility with plants; it does not validate a particular
plant caller or assembly. `extract_canonical_tss()` is an optional stricter
helper and reports genes with missing or ambiguous selections.
